inlines.v: Battery Materials & Cells: Li-ion cells & packs (joint); Natural graphite (joint). Permanent Magnets & Drive Systems: Rare-earth permanent magnets (joint); Ferrite & other magnets (joint). Wind & Hydropower Equipment: Wind blades & hubs (India->US). Grid Equipment & Conductors: Copper smelting & refining (joint).

Recognise trusted partner supply of reactor parts; electrolysers; sensors & controller parts in procurement and content rules. Common anti-circumvention rules for li-ion cells & packs and rare-earth permanent magnets and ferrite & other magnets. Bind market access for wind blades & hubs. Keep uranium/fuel extraction: aggregated low-coverage sub-sectors (spent fuel & nuclear scrap, uranium ores); transformers; blade core wood (balsa) open to global sourcing.
Upgrade DFC operations in India under the 2022 Investment Incentive Agreement: sector strategy, reciprocal commitments, a KPI dashboard and an annual review. No new MOU.
Do not create a new bilateral energy MOU or a free-standing MEA institution. Do not defend AC generators as a bilateral priority. Do not defend Automatic controllers as a bilateral priority.

Of 142 technology x stage cells and electro-industrial nodes assessed for the pair, 24 show an active complementarity (a supplier meeting the other's need, a shared chokepoint, a capacity-constrained trusted supplier or a chain specialisation), 5 direct competition and 86 no strategic case. The relationship is not one of general similarity: most of the electro-industrial base needs no bilateral intervention.

AIB strategic roles: US Demand & Market Anchor (primary), Coordination / Bridge Hub (primary), Capital & Investment Anchor (primary), Scale Manufacturing & Integration Platform (secondary), Specialized Technology & Manufacturing Anchor (secondary); India Coordination / Bridge Hub (primary), Development & Scale-Up Platform (secondary), Specialized Technology & Manufacturing Anchor (secondary).

India supplies wind blades & hubs, nuclear special materials where the US is short; the US supplies reactor parts, electrolysers, sensors & controller parts, electric furnaces & heating where India is short; the two share exposure to the same coercive supplier in li-ion cells & packs, natural graphite, copper smelting & refining, rare-earth permanent magnets, ferrite & other magnets, where neither can supply the other and the answer is joint demand, finance and third-country capacity.

From the AIB roles, the US brings demand and offtake, coordination across allied chains, capital; India brings coordination across allied chains, sites for development and scale-up, specialised technology and manufacturing. Public finance runs through DOE LPO, DoW OSC, DFC, EXIM on the US side and India Exim Bank on the India side. The trade is market access and demand certainty for trusted capacity.

This section sets out what already exists before anything new is proposed. Facts are from the curated evidence layer (accessed 2026-11-13); items marked partial or unverified rest on secondary sources and should be confirmed before citation.
India's memberships in OSI's economic-security agreements table: IPEF, MSP.

The two National Security Advisors held the inaugural iCET meeting on 31 Jan 2023, covering semiconductor supply chains, AI, quantum, space and defence innovation, and named rare-earth processing and advanced materials for future cooperation. The February 2025 leaders' statement carries this agenda forward under TRUST and does not mention iCET.

Quad leaders committed to identify and address gaps in manufacturing capacity for clean-energy technologies, focusing on solar PV, hydrogen electrolysers and EV batteries. They adopted joint principles for clean-energy supply chains and planned a public-private Quad Clean Energy Supply Chain Conference.

Australia was to open applications in Nov 2024 for the AUD 50m (about US$34m at Sep 2024 rates) programme supporting solar-panel, electrolyser and battery supply-chain projects in the Indo-Pacific. India committed US$2m to solar projects in Fiji, Comoros, Madagascar and Seychelles, and Japan US$122m to renewable projects. Awards and 2025-26 activity are not stated.

Leaders re-committed to the Energy Security Partnership covering oil, gas and civil nuclear, aimed to make the US a leading supplier of crude, petroleum products and LNG to India, backed India's full IEA membership and agreed to expand strategic oil-reserve arrangements. The statement does not mention the earlier Strategic Clean Energy Partnership.

Both countries are MSP members (India joined in June 2023) and committed in February 2025 to promote investment along the critical-mineral value chain through it. The MSP was succeeded by FORGE at the February 2026 Critical Minerals Ministerial.

India joined the US-led Pax Silica initiative on AI, semiconductor and critical-mineral supply chains on 20 Feb 2026, after being left out of the December 2025 launch group; the initiative now has about 27 signatories including the EU.
Quad foreign ministers adopted a framework to mobilise up to $20bn for secure critical-mineral supply chains; a separate July 2025 Quad initiative is mentioned only in passing and not sourced.
Launched July 2025 and framework adopted May 2026 to mobilise up to US$20bn of public and private support for mining, processing and recycling; no project list.

On 7 Oct 2026 the trade ministers of Argentina, Australia, Canada, the EU, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Poland, Turkiye, the UK and the US signed a statement committing to new sectoral platforms on structural excess capacity. The platforms start with autos and EVs, batteries, chemicals, foundational semiconductors and solar panels, and officials are to meet at technical level before December 2026 to draft terms of reference and share data.

Secretary Rubio's second India visit of 2026 focused on energy cooperation, commercial investment and economic ties: he met Jaishankar in Mumbai, toured Reliance's 1.4m b/d Jamnagar refinery and urged more refining of Venezuelan crude. No purchase commitments were announced.
In the OSI energy basket, US imported US$15.4bn from India and India imported US$13.6bn from US (bilateral flows 2024, summed over the technology x stage cells).

Leaders set Mission 500 to more than double bilateral trade to US$500bn by 2030 and planned to negotiate the first tranche of a multi-sector BTA by fall 2025. That deadline passed without a signed tranche.

USTR Greer travelled to New Delhi in June 2026 to discuss the Joint Statement and the Interim Agreement. By late October 2026 no deal had been concluded; India's foreign ministry said both sides reaffirmed their commitment to concluding one, and a former Indian ambassador said India was waiting for the US to formalise its tariff positions.

In February 2026 Commerce set preliminary countervailing duties on solar cells and panels from India, Indonesia and Laos following a 2025 petition by US manufacturers. Company rates, the anti-dumping preliminaries and the final Commerce and ITC determinations are not stated in the source.

Leaders launched the COMPACT (Catalyzing Opportunities for Military Partnership, Accelerated Commerce & Technology) as the umbrella for defence, trade, energy and technology outcomes, and welcomed about US$7.35bn of ongoing Indian investment in the US, including Novelis aluminium in Alabama and Kentucky, JSW steel in Texas and Ohio and Epsilon Advanced Materials battery materials in North Carolina.

TRUST (Transforming the Relationship Utilizing Strategic Technology) covers AI, semiconductors, quantum, biotech, energy and space and commits to trusted supply chains for semiconductors and critical minerals. Under it the leaders launched the Strategic Mineral Recovery initiative to recover and process lithium, cobalt and rare earths from aluminium, coal-mining and oil-and-gas streams; no budget or project list is given.

India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on all US industrial goods and many farm goods. The US set an 18% reciprocal rate and, once the Interim Agreement is concluded, will remove it on generic pharmaceuticals, gems and aircraft parts, lift Section 232 tariffs on certain aircraft parts and give India a preferential quota for auto parts. Both sides agreed to align on economic security, including inbound and outbound investment reviews and export controls, and either side may modify its commitments if the other's tariffs change.

India intends to purchase US$500bn of US energy products, aircraft and parts, precious metals, technology products and coking coal over five years, and trade in GPUs and other data-centre goods is to rise significantly. No annual schedule or enforcement mechanism is stated.

First Solar commissioned its Tamil Nadu module factory in 2024, its only plant in India, alongside US plants in Ohio, Alabama and Louisiana. Its capacity is reported at about 3.3 GW a year but is not stated in the source.
DFC extended a US$250m loan to Tata Power Solar to build a solar-cell manufacturing plant in India, reported as a US Quad contribution. Plant capacity and disbursement are not stated in the source.
DFC extended a US$500m loan to First Solar to build and operate a solar-module manufacturing plant in India, reported as a US Quad contribution. Capacity is not stated in the source.

The February 2025 leaders' statement lists Epsilon Advanced Materials' manufacture of critical battery materials in North Carolina among ongoing Indian investments in the US. The plant is reported elsewhere as a synthetic-graphite anode facility; its value and construction status are not stated in the source.

Vikram Solar's chairman said in December 2025 the company was evaluating setting up manufacturing in the United States. It commissioned a 5 GW module plant at Vallam, Tamil Nadu, in November 2025 and listed in August 2025 after a Rs 2,079 crore (about US$236m) IPO; no US site or capacity has been announced.
Unverified items are left out of this section; they stay in the evidence register (evidence_register.csv) and the evidence layer.

Working channels today: US-India civil nuclear cooperation (123 Agreement of 2008, Kovvada AP1000 track, Part 810 transfers) (a project pipeline); Minerals Security Partnership and FORGE (finance); DFC operations in India under the 2022 Investment Incentive Agreement (a project pipeline and finance). What the relationship lacks: no cross-sector KPI dashboard or review cycle; no bilateral mechanism covers SC-MAGNETS; USIN-M8 has no published project pipeline.

EO 14329, signed 6 Aug 2025, added a 25% ad valorem duty on goods of India because India imported Russian oil; it applied from 27 Aug 2025 and lifted the combined US tariff on many Indian goods to 50% with the 25% reciprocal rate. EO 14384 terminated it from 7 Feb 2026.

From 12:01 a.m. EST on 7 Feb 2026 products of India are no longer subject to the 25% Russian-oil duty and HTS headings 9903.01.84-89 are terminated. Commerce, with State and Treasury, monitors whether India resumes direct or indirect imports of Russian oil and may recommend reimposing the 25% duty.

The White House said on 9 Feb 2026 that the IEEPA reciprocal tariff on India would fall from 25% to 18% under the trade framework. On 20 Feb 2026 the Supreme Court held that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs, so the 18% rate lapsed and IEEPA duties became refundable (about US$81bn refunded to all importers by July 2026).

After the ruling a 10% Section 122 surcharge applied to Indian and almost all other imports from 24 Feb 2026 for 150 days. The Court of International Trade found it unjustified on 7 May 2026 (relief limited to the plaintiffs and stayed by the Federal Circuit in June 2026), and it expired on 24 Jul 2026.

In February 2026 Commerce set preliminary countervailing duties on solar cells and panels from India, Indonesia and Laos following a 2025 petition by US manufacturers. Company rates, the anti-dumping preliminaries and the final Commerce and ITC determinations are not stated in the source.

USTR took final Section 301 action on 60 economies on 23 Jul 2026. India is one of 17 economies at 10% (those with, or committed to, a forced-labour import ban) rather than the 12.5% default. Exemptions cover scarce raw materials and products whose tariffing would disrupt the economy. The duties replaced the Section 122 surcharge from 24 Jul 2026.

In September 2026 the House voted to advance a bill authorising 100% tariffs on countries that buy Russian oil and gas, which would cover India, while extending Iran sanctions. Enactment status is not stated in the source.

Joint bets resting on a node need inherited from its cell (a proxy): Li-ion cells & packs; Rare-earth permanent magnets; Wind blades & hubs; Copper smelting & refining.
Evidence-led compacts (OSI cannot see the partner's capability in trade data): Solar Manufacturing.

India has no listed trade position (under 1% of world supply) at nodes where the US has material demand: li-ion cells & packs, natural graphite, rare-earth permanent magnets, ferrite & other magnets, electrolysers, uranium/fuel extraction: aggregated low-coverage sub-sectors (spent fuel & nuclear scrap, uranium ores), uranium conversion & enrichment, nuclear reactors & enrichment machinery, accumulator parts & separators, lithium chemicals, pv cover glass, heat pumps & ac units, solar thermal water heaters, gallium, germanium & indium, power semiconductors, electric two-wheelers & works trucks, blade core wood (balsa), pgms (iridium, ruthenium). Trade data miss capability that is owned abroad or sold at home, so these nodes cannot show complementarity even where corporate evidence suggests it.
Low-evidence units among the active states: none.

Trade data understate concentration at uranium conversion & enrichment: enrichment is sold as a service under long-term contracts, so goods trade understates Russia's share of world enrichment capacity (roughly 40%), and the 2024 US ban on Russian low-enriched uranium imports makes trusted capacity the binding constraint.

Trade data understate concentration at gallium, germanium & indium: China's export controls since 2023 cut its recorded exports, so 2024 trade understates its share of primary gallium and germanium output (the large majority of world supply).
